body:
im not familiar with "funcname" and "lineno" tokens in logging, and IIUC from what you have there it looks like it's doing some kind of traceback inspection when you emit a log line, which means that no logging helper functions of any kind can be used by any application.   if I have all that right, that's unfortunately an unreasonable constraint so I wouldnt see any way to fix this.   But this is just my reading in the last 30 seconds, so correct me if im not getting it right.

I would recommend setting a separate formatter for the sqlalchemy.engine namespace that has the prefixing information you want pre-formatted.

[funcname and lineno are part of the Python `LogRecord` object, next to 'message'](https://docs.python.org/3/library/logging.html#logrecord-objects), which is of course the text that is usually shown on stdout. However all the other fields are on an equal level, even if not shown. For my use case we forward all logging records to a graylog server, where they are aggregated. All sqlalchemy related log messages are shown as coming from the same file, the same function, and the same line, although it is clear that they come from separate log calls. This makes it hard to filter for relevant messages.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2102431/150995759-f41d642d-5f26-42f1-a477-3f607e1badcf.png)

Judging from the code the only reason these helper functions exist is to include prefixes into the log message, specifically a [`logging_token`](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/14/core/engines.html#setting-per-connection-sub-engine-tokens). That token is then prefixed into the message.

This is unfortunate, as a cleaner way would have been to leave the message alone, add the token as an [_`extra`_](https://docs.python.org/3/library/logging.html#logging.Logger.debug) field to the log message (example from the Python logging documentation):
```python
d = {'clientip': '192.168.0.1', 'user': 'fbloggs'}
logger = logging.getLogger('tcpserver')
logger.warning('Protocol problem: %s', 'connection reset', extra=d)
```
That way the field can be directly filtered on, the original message is retained - and there would not be a need for a helper function, therefore you'd also get the correct logging context in the message (There's no need to add the field to every individual message, [a `LoggerAdapter` can do that for you](https://docs.python.org/3/howto/logging-cookbook.html#adding-contextual-information-to-your-logging-output)).

I guess the main underlying issue is that people weren't aware that the logging framework does a lot more underneath the hood than just carry a flat string...

I'm happy to have a look into upgrading SQLAlchemy to make full use of python logging framework features. It would probably be incompatible with the current `logging_token` functionality though.

I'm pretty aware the logging framework is quite extensible so I would request that we refrain from talking about decisions being "unfortunate" or otherwise commenting on the relative ignorance of the developers, kind of makes it difficult for me to be open to your suggestions.  sorry

It seems that no-one knows all the stuff that the logging module can do.

From https://docs.python.org/3/library/logging.html#logging.Logger.debug it seems we can just set `stacklevel=2` to fix this

> I'll have a go at making a PR. And if at some point someone really wants to put in the work to have extra fields then that can be done separately.

sounds like a plan!

i dont really recall why i have it implemented with that extra formatting, i'd need to review what the docs /changelog / rationale for "logging token" are.  i think the idea was that i didnt want a blank pair of brackets in the log message if there were no "logging token" but I could have just formatted it with "[]".

but otherwise with _log_info and _log_debug, those methods are also called from CursorResult and maybe elsewhere too.  that is, the purpose of these methods is to abstract away additional logging behaviors that the Connection wants to maintain.     So yes, you can make a LoggerAdapter or otherwise inject using systems like that.  overall though, if we did that here and made sure we invoked from the logger directly where it's used, i dont know of an automated way to prevent it from being changed again three years later unless we add some new tests that asserts the formatting of the messages including code lines (we have a test suite for logging that already runs tests like this, so I think we should add to it).

so if we can in fact just stick a stacklevel in , let's do that, but yes the thing I'm actually doing in _log_info / _log_debug looks kind of clumsy in any case so I'm open to cleaning that up also.

@Anthchirp  if you want to try asserting a particular log output for these fields, so that this doesnt break later, see if you can add to https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/main/test/engine/test_logging.py , where in places like https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/main/test/engine/test_logging.py#L659 you can see we are using logging handlers to capture log messages and we then assert that they have a desired format.

issue.title: Fix up Python logging metadata
issue.body:
<!-- Provide a general summary of your proposed changes in the Title field above -->

### Description
<!-- Describe your changes in detail -->
Log messages emitted via `sqlalchemy.engine.base` and `sqlalchemy.log` may
report incorrect function names and line numbers, as they may be based
off a helper function stack frame. Add, and increment, the `stacklevel`
keyword argument to function calls to ensure that helper functions are
not themselves visible in the log records.

Fixes #7612


Open questions:
I don't know in what context `sqlalchemy.log` is otherwise used. I'm not entirely convinced that the stacklevel logic implemented here is correct in _all_ cases.
